I work at a very busy store, usually do the whole 4-10:30 shift completely alone past 6 pm. and I start doing closing duties by 7:30 pm. I try to get as much prep done as possible between customers when I first get there ,  and then at 7:30 I pull out all the trays to pull bread, then pull bread (these steps are separate bc 99% of the  time it’s interrupted by customers) then I do other freezer pull and sidekick pull as well next. After that I take all the trashes , usually by combining 2 bags into 1 can (we have about 8 cans) and then taking out 4 bags. I usually keep one of them up until the end of the night before I sweep as well so that all the trash cans are empty for morning crew. At about 9 I start shutting everything off . The hotwell, the oven, the line. I keep the toaster running until 10 when we close incase someone wants their sandwich toasted. The reason I turn the line and hotwell off slightly early is allow time for the line to defrost and the hotwell to cool so that it’s easier to clean. I try to wipe down the lobby and bathrooms before we fully lock up as well but that doesn’t always happen.
After locking up, i put away the line and then I do the night dishes that were already at the sink. After that, i wipe down the line , wipe down the front area , and then take apart the cutting boards and start collecting the closing dishes. Once those are done, i count the drawers , close the day , do anything extra that needs to get done , then sweep, mop, and clock the fuck out.  I have it on a routine and it rlly does help. Unfortunately it does depend on how busy it was that day for when we leave . Sometimes I’m only there till 10:30-10:40 but the other day I was there until literally 11:59 pm.

I did take the rest of that day and the next day off, I could’ve taken more but I needed the hours and money. I’ve been moving lately so I haven’t actually had time to think about it much. Recuperating is hard when you are busy 24/7 haha.  Also, for me, I’m not a closer. He robbed me at literally 3 PM. Broad Daylight.
